summary: This article explains how hummingbirds hover on fast-beating wings, feed on nectar, save energy at night, carry pollen between flowers, build tiny nests, and make long trips.
introduce: Ask students to share a small problem they solved this week and how they solved it, and write two examples in a Problem | Solution chart on the board. Tell them that “Hummingbirds: Tiny Fliers” also has a problem and a solution to find.

keyTerms.def: to stay in one place in the air
to travel a long way from one area to another, often each season

challengeTerms.def: all the chemical processes a body uses to turn food into energy
a regular journey that animals make from one region to another
an animal that carries pollen between flowers, helping plants produce seeds

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a tiny animal can do things that big animals cannot? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain two ways a hummingbird's body or habits help it deal with.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review species, hover, and migrate, and let weak readers fill in a simple Problem | Solution chart with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses metabolism, migration, and pollinator to suggest a second solution to the problem and judge which works better.
